$comment: Deploy contract consumed by the aef-deploy skill. Separate from .servyn/project.json (build topology, read at a pinned SHA by the webhook fan-out) so a deploy-runbook edit can never perturb a production build. See servyn/docs/servyn-deploy-contract.md.

apps.name: tetris-game

healthChecks.note: Static nginx serve. A 200 on / only proves nginx is up; also confirm the served HTML actually changed when the deploy was meant to change it, since a stale container will answer 200 identically.

rollback.note: Buildpack app, no retained image. Roll back by deploying the prior good SHA (push it to a temporary branch and deploy that, then delete the temp branch). Do NOT force-push master.

apps.notes:
THE BRANCH IS `master`, NOT `main`. This is the single most likely way to get this app wrong — every other app in the fleet except reliq deploys from `main`, so the habit is to assume it. Verified against the live host 2026-08-19: `App deploy source metadata: https://github.com/sheistenberg/tetris-game#6995246`, deployBranch `master`.

No build step and no tests exist — it is a static site (index.html + style.css + script.js served by nginx:alpine, per the root Dockerfile). There is deliberately no preDeployGate: `docker build` on the host IS the only gate, and inventing a gate command that does not exist in the repo would fail every deploy. If a build or test step is ever added, declare it here.

No `port` is declared because none is set on the host (`ports:report` is empty) — the Dockerfile's `EXPOSE 80` default is correct and sufficient for this app. Do not add a port mapping speculatively; the port-regression gotcha that affects prebuilt-image apps does not apply to a buildpack app with no explicit mapping.

Never run enable_ssl / dokku letsencrypt. Cloudflare terminates TLS at the edge for *.nexrahq.com and the HTTP-01 challenge will fail behind it.
